strategy.summary: openapi.yaml changed: GET /orders/{id} now returns `total` (Money: amount + currency) instead of `totalCents`, and `status` may be `cancelled`; POST /orders/{id}/cancel was added (200 Order, 404 unknown order, 409 already cancelled). The tests must assert the new getOrder shape and cover cancelOrder's success and each documented error, against the real app started in-process as the existing vitest specs do.
inScope: GET /orders/{id} 200 body (total replaces totalCents; status cancelled)
outOfScope: Operations the spec didn't change (products, POST /orders); the existing GET /orders/{id} 404 test stays as is
assumptions: The real app runs in-process (createApp on port 0) as in the existing specs; nothing is faked.
The order total's currency is USD: the catalogue prices are in USD cents and the store records currency 'USD' on each order; the spec allows USD or EUR.

Tests stay in test/orders.test.js beside the getOrder tests, following its in-file setup; the existing test changes only its totalCents assertion; each test places its own order so no test depends on another's.

risks.description: Existing getOrder test asserts the removed totalCents and would fail or keep checking the old contract
risks.mitigation: TC1 updates it to the Money total with the same exact-body check

risks.description: Cancel endpoint untested: a wrong status code or body shape would go unnoticed by clients
risks.mitigation: TC2–TC5 cover 200, the cancelled status on read, 404 and 409

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /orders/{id} returns 200 with the order's id, productId, quantity, status and total {amount in cents, currency}, and no totalCents
GET /orders/{id} of a cancelled order returns status 'cancelled'
POST /orders/{id}/cancel of a placed order returns 200 with the Order, status 'cancelled'
POST /orders/{id}/cancel of an unknown order returns 404 with an Error body {error: string}
POST /orders/{id}/cancel of an already cancelled order returns 409 with an Error body {error: string}

testCases.title: returns an order with its total
steps: Place an order for product 1 (2499 cents), quantity 2
testCases.expected: 200, body equals {id, productId: 1, quantity: 2, status: 'placed', total: {amount: 4998, currency: 'USD'}} (no totalCents)
testCases.rationale: getOrder changed: totalCents removed, total (Money) added; updates the existing test at test/orders.test.js:48 to the new contract

testCases.title: returns a cancelled order with status cancelled
steps: Place an order for product 3, quantity 1
testCases.expected: 200, body equals {id, productId: 3, quantity: 1, status: 'cancelled', total: {amount: 699, currency: 'USD'}}
testCases.rationale: getOrder changed: status now allows 'cancelled', which a caller sees after cancelling

testCases.title: cancels a placed order
steps: Place an order for product 3, quantity 2
testCases.expected: 200, content-type application/json, body equals {id, productId: 3, quantity: 2, status: 'cancelled', total: {amount: 1398, currency: 'USD'}}

testCases.title: is 404 when cancelling an unknown order
is 409 when cancelling an order already cancelled
steps: Place an order for product 3, quantity 1

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services: each spec starts the app in-process on an OS-chosen port with its own in-memory store.

cases.title: POST /orders refuses a quantity under one
POST /orders is 404 for an unknown product
POST /orders is 409 when the stock is short
GET /orders/{id} returns an order with its total
GET /orders/{id} returns a cancelled order with status cancelled
GET /orders/{id} is 404 for an unknown order
POST /orders/{id}/cancel is 404 when cancelling an unknown order
POST /orders/{id}/cancel is 409 when cancelling an order already cancelled

review.standard: General test automation standards: a helper two tests need goes once in a helper (Reuse the repo's helpers)
review.summary: The change adds a `cancelOrder` helper (line 23) but writes the same `fetch(`${base}/orders/${id}/cancel`, { method: 'POST' })` inline again at lines 85, 98 and 106.
review.failureScenario: If the cancel call changes (say it gains a header or body), someone updates `cancelOrder` and misses the three inline copies at lines 85, 98 and 106. The tests then send two different requests to the same operation. Using `cancelOrder(id)` / `cancelOrder(999)` keeps the path the spec names, so TestForge can still place the call.

review.standard: General test automation standards: setup helpers check each response's status and fail with its body
review.summary: The new tests read `id` from `placeOrder(...)` without checking that the call returned 201. When placement fails, the test fails later with a misleading status mismatch.
review.failureScenario: Say POST /orders starts refusing product 3 (the stock runs out, or validation changes). `id` is then undefined, the cancel goes to /orders/undefined/cancel and gets the router's 404, and the failure reads `expected 404 to be 200` on the cancel step, not the real cause. This happens at lines 63, 84 and 104. It copies the existing pattern at line 50, so it is a cleanup, not a wrong pass.
